text:
Brock Boeser has a point in five straight games, three of them goals, and he is closing in on 500 career points, every one as a Canuck (The Hockey News has been tracking the milestones). On a team that has lost nine of ten, he has been one of the few things that works: seven goals and 11 power-play points in 20 games.

The finishing is running ahead of the chances. Seven goals on 4.4 expected means a 22% shooting rate, against 13% last season, and that rarely lasts. The bigger worry is at five-on-five, where Vancouver gets only 36% of the expected goals with him on the ice, more than six points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey flagged the same thing last season (opponents created more with him out there, bottom 8% of forwards), while noting he plays with weaker teammates than most. Boeser at his best is a shooter who gets fed, and Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis loved one recent Filip Hronek point shot: "Low and hard in the perfect spot for Boeser to tip it home." That part of his game is still producing.
headline: Boeser's streak is real, the finishing runs hot
